layout_structure.title_text: Dual Prototype Evolving for Test-Time Generalization of Vision-Language Models
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide follows a centered title slide layout on a plain white background. At the top left, the Carnegie Mellon University School of Computer Science logo is displayed, while the Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) logo is positioned at the top right. The main title is centered in a large, bold, black font. Below the title, the names of four authors are listed horizontally. Underneath the authors, the institutional affiliation 'School of Computer Science, Carnegie Mellon University' is centered, followed by a line of monospaced email addresses. Near the bottom, there is information about the poster session and a clickable project page URL. The slide also features UI elements from a presentation viewer, including large circular navigation arrows on the left and right sides, a control bar at the bottom center indicating 'Slide 1 / 9', and a page number '1' in the bottom right corner. The text density is light, focusing on key identifying information.

The slide features a large, bold, dark red title 'DPE Overview' at the top-left and the 'NEURAL INFORMATION PROCESSING SYSTEMS' logo at the top-right. The main body is dominated by a complex, multi-stage flowchart illustrating the DPE architecture, flowing from left to right. On the left, three input categories are shown: 'Text Descriptions', 'High-Confidence Samples' (with small images of dogs, cats, and cars), and 'Augmented Test Images'. These lead into 'Text Encoder' and 'Image Encoder' blocks, which are annotated with snowflake icons (indicating frozen weights) or fire icons (indicating trainable components). The center of the diagram depicts the initialization and evolution of 'Textual Prototypes' and 'Visual Prototypes', connected by a circular 'L_align' loss term. To the right of this, the process continues through 'Predictions of All Views', 'Confidence Selection', and an 'Average' step that produces a final output and an 'L_aug' loss. On the far right, two separate panels visualize 'Textual Prototype Evolution' and 'Visual Prototype Evolution' using node-link diagrams and a clock icon to signify temporal change. A two-line summary sentence is placed at the bottom-left, and the page number '3' is at the bottom-right. The overall text density is moderate, with a clean white background and a color-coded scheme for different data modalities.

The slide features a large, complex architectural diagram centered between a top title and a bottom summary text. The title 'DPE Overview' is positioned in a large, bold, dark red font at the top-left, while the 'NEURAL INFORMATION PROCESSING SYSTEMS' logo with its purple dot pattern is at the top-right. The central diagram flows from left to right, starting with input sources on the left: 'Text Descriptions', 'High-Confidence Samples' (images of dogs, cats, and cars), and 'Augmented Test Images'. These inputs pass through frozen encoders, indicated by snowflake icons. The middle section illustrates 'Textual Prototypes' and 'Visual Prototypes' undergoing a 'Prototype Evolving' process with an 'L_align' loss. To the right of the main flow, two separate panels show the 'Textual Prototype Evolution' and 'Visual Prototype Evolution' over time, marked by clock icons. The final stage of the main diagram shows 'Predictions of All Views', 'Confidence Selection', and an 'Average' step leading to final class scores and an 'L_aug' loss. A two-line summary paragraph at the bottom explains the method's use of prototypes and CLIP. The slide has a white background with a page number '3' in the bottom-right corner.

The slide follows a clean, single-column layout on a white background. The title 'Prototype Evolution' is prominently displayed in the top-left corner in a large, bold, dark red font. In the top-right corner, there is a logo for 'NEURAL INFORMATION PROCESSING SYSTEMS' featuring a purple abstract neural network icon. The main body of the slide starts with an introductory paragraph. Below this, the content is structured into two main hierarchical sections: 'Textual Prototype Evolution' and 'Visual Prototype Evolution'. Each section is introduced by a bolded heading with a square bullet point and contains two sub-bullets marked with small circles. The text is left-aligned, and the hierarchical structure uses indentation to organize the information. A small page number '4' is visible in the bottom-right corner. The slide has a moderate text density with significant white space, making it easy to read.

layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a clean, white background with a large bold title 'Experiments' in dark red at the top-left. Below the title, a single bullet point marked with a small red square introduces the content: 'Performance comparisons on robustness to natural distribution shifts'. The main body of the slide is occupied by a large, detailed table comparing various methods across multiple datasets. The table is split into two horizontal blocks, one for 'CLIP-ResNet-50' and another for 'CLIP-ViT-B/16'. Each block lists several baseline methods and the proposed 'DPE (Ours)' method, which is highlighted with a light gray background to draw attention. The table columns represent different ImageNet variants (ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-S) and average performance metrics (Average, OOD Average). In the top-right corner, there is a purple logo for 'NEURAL INFORMATION PROCESSING SYSTEMS'. A small page number '6' is located at the bottom-right corner. The text density is moderate to high due to the numerical data in the table.

layout_structure.layout_description: The slide has a clean white background with a large, bold, dark red title 'Experiments' positioned at the top-left. This table is organized into two main horizontal sections, each representing a different backbone architecture (CLIP-ResNet-50 and CLIP-ViT-B/16). Each section lists several methods in the first column, including the authors' proposed 'DPE (Ours)', which is highlighted with a light gray background. The subsequent columns represent various datasets (Aircraft, Caltech, Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, Flower, Food101, Pets, SUN397, UCF101) and an 'Average' column. The table is filled with numerical performance data, with the best results in each column bolded for emphasis. In the top-right corner, there is a purple decorative logo for 'NEURAL INFORMATION PROCESSING SYSTEMS'. A small page number '7' is visible in the bottom-right corner. The text density is high due to the extensive numerical information presented in the table.

The slide uses a white background with a large, bold, dark red title 'Experiments' at the top-left. The content is organized into three distinct blocks, each introduced by a subheading with a small red square icon. The top-left block contains a data table titled 'Efficiency comparison on ImageNet' comparing six methods across testing time and accuracy metrics. The top-right block features a table titled 'Ablation study on different textual prototype evolution rules' that includes a column for mathematical update formulas. The bottom half of the slide, titled 'More ablation studies', displays three figures side-by-side: a 3D bar chart on the left showing accuracy across two parameters, a grouped bar chart in the center comparing refinement methods across three datasets, and a line graph on the right showing accuracy trends relative to a scale factor. A purple dot-pattern logo for 'NEURAL INFORMATION PROCESSING SYSTEMS' is in the top-right corner, and the page number '8' is at the bottom-right. The text density is moderate to dense, utilizing a color palette of teal, green, orange, and pink for the graphical data.
